units.title: Polynomial Gaussian ridges have one dimension-independent L2 norm
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, and p any real polynomial. Put phi(z)=p(z), gamma1=N(0,1), gammaE=stdGaussian(E), and U={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Then phi genuinely belongs to L2(gamma1). Define b=norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)}+1. One has b>0, and every actual ridge x↦phi(<w,x>) for w in U genuinely belongs to L2(gammaE), with norm exactly norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)} and hence at most b. The one base norm and the same b serve every direction and dimension. Neither positive dimension, a nonzero polynomial nor evenness is required; the feature conclusions are vacuous when U is empty. No feature moment, covariance or uniform bound is assumed.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space; its measurable structure is Borel.
p is any finite real polynomial. The Gaussian measures are actual standard Gaussian laws, and feature weights range over the literal unit-norm subtype.

steps.title: Produce polynomial moments
steps.text: The actual scalar Gaussian has every finite moment. Thus z^n belongs to L2 since its squared absolute value is |z|^(2n). Finite polynomial induction, addition and coefficient scaling produce L2 membership of phi; no moment premise is introduced.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

steps.title: Identify the actual projection law
steps.text: A continuous linear functional of the standard Gaussian is Gaussian with mean zero and variance equal to its squared dual norm. The inner-product functional at a unit vector has norm one, so the pushforward is exactly gamma1.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

steps.title: Transport the genuine L2 class
steps.text: This measurable projection preserves the indicated measures. Pull back phi and its actual almost-everywhere class. The induced L2 pullback is an isometry, proving membership and equality of norms simultaneously.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

steps.title: Choose one positive common bound
steps.text: A norm is nonnegative, so adding one makes b strictly positive. The exact isometry gives the same bound for every unit weight, with no dimension or direction in its definition.
steps.lean: The adjacent initially folded Lean contains the exact statement and proof of this step.

boundary: The Gaussian law and unit norm are essential. This is not a theorem for arbitrary rotation-invariant heavy-tailed laws or unbounded directions.
No pointwise feature bound is claimed. No label moment, averaging over arbitrary parameter laws, global risk first variation or stochastic convergence is supplied.

tests.scope: Actual non-even polynomial on opposite unit directions, zero polynomial and zero-dimensional base membership.
